title: The Contact of the Green Zone
premise: Petra Thackeray, a deniable fixer for the Green Zone's unofficial embassy, receives a call on a burner that was destroyed years ago—the voice belongs to her former handler, Elias Voss, officially dead for three years. Voss reveals that a faction inside the mission is orchestrating a chemical 'accident' at a diplomatic summit to trigger a power grab, and that Petra's name is on the cleanup list. Torn between loyalty to the institution that made her and the truth Voss offers, Petra races to expose the plot while evading the colleagues sent to erase her. In the end, she chooses justice over the mission, leaking the evidence publicly at the cost of her invisibility and walking away as the embassy burns down around her.
about_author: Juniper Crane is the pseudonym of a former diplomatic security contractor who writes what she can't say aloud. She lives somewhere unlisted, and her thrillers are praised for their unnervingly accurate tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A routine job—silencing a whistleblower—unravels when her old burner, supposedly incinerated, lights up with Voss's voice. He claims the whistleblower was a decoy and Petra herself is the next loose end. The emotional beat is vertigo: everything Petra trusted about her own history cracks open, and paranoia replaces professional calm.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Body Count
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with a tense midpoint scene from Deputy Chief Arden Kessler, her current handler, who quietly green-lights her surveillance. Petra verifies a fragment of Voss's claim—a shipment manifest for the summit's 'fire suppression' system. The beat is betrayal: she realizes the institution she'd kill for is already killing, and she must decide which side of the manifest she stands on.

chapters.title: Forty Hours to an Accident
chapters.summary: Alternating Petra and Kessler POVs. Petra breaks into the embassy's black annex to copy the operational file while Kessler closes the net, deploying her former teammates as hunters. A brutal chase through the old quarter ends with Petra wounded and Voss captured. The beat is desperation: with her ally gone and the clock burning down, Petra has one move left and no permission to make it.

chapters.title: What the Green Zone Buried
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the summit, she triggers the chemical release's abort sequence and broadcasts the annex file to every press desk in the city as Kessler's team closes in. Voss, traded for leverage, dies buying her ninety seconds. The beat is costly vindication: the attack fails, the embassy implodes in scandal, and Petra walks out unnamed—finally visible to everyone who matters, and free.
